name: bowerrc

cwd.description: The directory from which bower should run. All relative paths will be calculated according to this setting.

directory.description: The directory from which bower should run. All relative paths will be calculated according to this setting.

json.description: A file path to the Bower configuration file

search.description: An array of URLs pointing to read-only Bower registries. A string means only one. When looking into the registry for an endpoint, Bower will query these registries by the specified order.

register.description: The URL to use when registering packages.

publish.description: The URL to use when publishing packages.

proxy.description: The proxy to use for http requests.

https-proxy.description: The proxy to use for https requests.

user-agent.description: Sets the User-Agent for each request made.

timeout.description: The timeout to be used when making requests in milliseconds.

strict-ssl.description: Whether or not to do SSL key validation when making requests via https.

ca.description: The CA certificates to be used, defaults to null. This is similar to the registry key, specifying each CA to use for each registry endpoint.

color.description: Enable or disable use of colors in the CLI output.

storage.description: Where to store persistent data, such as cache, needed by bower.

tmp.description: Where to store temporary files and folders

interactive.description: Makes bower interactive, prompting whenever necessary

resolvers.description: Identifies pluggable resolvers to be used for locating and fetching packages

shallowCloneHosts.description: Whitelists hosts which are known to support shallow cloning

scripts.description: Contains custom hooks used to trigger other automated tools

preinstall.description: A script to run before install

postinstall.description: A script to run after install

preuninstall.description: A script to run before uninstall

ignoredDependencies.description: Bower will ignore these dependencies when resolving packages

description:
Our Bower environment is set up for the project located at **/home/user/my-app**, using **vendor/bower_components** as the component folder and the default **bower.json** file for package definitions. We have turned analytics off and enabled colored CLI output. Interactive prompts are disabled, and the client identifies itself as **my-bower-client/1.0.0**. All HTTP requests go through **http://proxy.example.com:8080**, while HTTPS traffic uses **https://secure‑proxy.example.com:8443**. SSL validation is enforced, with the certificate authority file **/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt**. Requests may take up to **120 000 ms** before timing out. Persistent data is stored under our home directory: packages in **/home/user/.bower/packages**, registry metadata in **/home/user/.bower/registry**, and link information in **/home/user/.bower/links**. Temporary files are written to **/tmp/bower**.

The registry configuration points to two search endpoints—**https://registry.bower.io** and **https://bower.herokuapp.com**—and uses **https://registry.bower.io/register** for registering packages and **https://registry.bower.io/publish** for publishing them. We rely on the built‑in resolvers **git**, **svn**, and **hg**, and we allow shallow cloning on **github.com**, **gitlab.com**, and **bitbucket.org**. Custom hook scripts are defined: a pre‑install step runs **npm run lint**, a post‑install step runs **npm run build**, and a pre‑uninstall step runs **npm run clean**. Bower will ignore the dependencies **jquery** and **bootstrap** during resolution. Finally, an extra custom property has been added for demonstration purposes with the value **“extra value for demonstration.”**
